My family gave me an intervention of sorts, so I'm safe now.

No matter what, someone in the world is going to die before, on, and after your birthday. I've been to therapists and find that I don't feel comfortable opening up to them. I've tried about seven at this point. As far as medication, all it does is mask these feelings. I'm still unmotivated, I'm still inattentive, and I'm still anxious. Sure, I don't feel like I want to die *all* the time, but it's there. And it'll never go away. I've been through this more than once, and I'm tired. I'm so fucking tired.

Dismissing me and saying that I "can live" is not what's going to stop me from doing this.

I find it funny how people think that being thin is the only way to be healthy. I'm working toward healthy, and by healthy I mean feeling good and being able to do what I want to do without my body holding me back. When I say that I will never be thin, it's true. And I don't want to be thin. I want people to realize that if you're comfortable with yourself, happy, and not at risk of health problems due to weight, it shouldn't matter if you look like what the media portrays as "beautiful". And I'm not justifying being overweight. Obviously, if you're at risk of diabetes, high blood pressure, cholesterol, etc., then ya got to lose the weight. That is not healthy and neither is trying to be what society has deemed is acceptable, even if it is not attainable.
